questions.asks: TAPC for a Windows program?
questions.note: Windows portable and installer releases (docs/binaries.md).

questions.asks: TAPC for a Linux program?
questions.note: Linux release exists; only Q1 is on the path.

questions.asks: TAPC for a macOS program?
questions.note: macOS release exists; only Q1 is on the path.

questions.asks: Another commercial OS?
A non-commercial OS?
Offered through an online platform?
questions.note: pairings.zerotwo.cloud; only Q1 is on the path.

questions.asks: English interface?
questions.note: English is the base locale (gettext).

questions.asks: English available straight after installation?
questions.note: English is the base locale and the fallback for every language but Dutch (lib/pairings_engine_web/locale.ex:39-44,73-75). The desktop build opens the system browser and follows its Accept-Language, so a Dutch browser opens in Dutch; English is one click away (Q9).

questions.asks: English selectable at run time?
questions.note: Language picker in the top bar of every page (lib/pairings_engine_web/components/layouts.ex:250,846-871; router.ex:232), and a per-account language. Off our path while Q8 is YES.

questions.asks: Non-English text inside the English interface?
questions.note: No non-English UI text found in the English catalogue. One placeholder said 'matricule'; it now says 'national ID' (fide_live.ex:784). The opt-in Belgian SWAR results-page export is Dutch by design: a federation upload document, not interface (federations/bel/swar_publish.ex:487-491).

questions.asks: Complete English manual or online help?
questions.note: An English user manual of fifteen chapters, covering every feature area, ships with the program (priv/manual/*.md, rendered by lib/pairings_engine/manual.ex) and opens from a Help link in the top bar of every page at /help (help_live.ex; tests manual_test.exs, help_live_test.exs). The maintainer judged it complete (2026-10-07); a Dutch translation ships alongside (priv/manual/nl).

questions.asks: Manual reachable from inside the program (e.g. F1)?
questions.note: The Help link is in the top bar of every page, signed in or not, and inside a tournament opens the chapter for the current tab (layouts.ex #topbar-help, help_path/1; help_live_test.exs 'opens the chapter that matches the tab').

questions.asks: Manual available separately (PDF / web link)?
questions.note: The manual is also a separate resource: plain Markdown files in priv/manual/ in the public repository (docs/manual/README.md points to them).

questions.asks: At least an essential-functions English manual?
questions.note: Covered by the in-app manual: rating lists (chapter 4), set-up and tie-breaks (3, 8), byes (5), pairings (6), printouts of results and standings (9) (priv/manual; help_live.ex).

questions.asks: Commit to completing a partial manual within a year?
questions.note: Not reached while Q11 is YES. If FIDE judges the manual partial: the maintainer's commitment to complete it within a year of the TAPC (5%). See docs/vcl4thp/questions.md.

questions.asks: Own pairing and tie-break engine?
questions.note: Ainalrami (pairing) + PairingsEngine.Standings (tie-breaks), both ours.

questions.asks: External engine?
External engine already inside a TAPC'd program?
Checker (PTC) and generator (RTG) available?
questions.note: ainalrami -c (checker) and -g (generator) in the public Apache-2.0 repository (deps/ainalrami/lib/ainalrami/cli.ex:339-349,1464-1526; README.md:222-229). No release binaries: clone, mix escript.build. The form's textbox text (how to get and run them) is still to write.

questions.asks: Checker has a free CLI?
questions.note: ainalrami <file> -c, free, exit codes 0 match / 1 differs / 2 not replayable (cli.ex:348-349,927-940). Built from source.

questions.asks: Checker reads TRF26 and reports wrong pairings per round AND standings that break the tie-breaks?
questions.note: Shipped in Ainalrami 0.30.0, pinned 0.35.0: reads TRF26 (202/212, 192, 250/260), replays every round, and re-ranks by the file's tie-break list, naming every wrong rank in columns 86-89 (cli.ex:948-974,1102-1145,1223-1245). Our own TRF26 exports now pass it, pairings and standings (test/pairings_engine/trf_checker_round_trip_test.exs) - except Baku tournaments, see Q106. Limits: individual colour differences are noted, not counted; a round robin exits 2 (not replayed).

questions.asks: Generator has a free CLI?
questions.note: ainalrami -g (cli.ex:339-340,428-475).

questions.asks: Generator has a free non-CLI interface?
questions.note: Not needed: Q22 is YES.

questions.asks: Generator configures players, rounds, each bye type, forfeit wins/losses, odd results, BAM, tie-break list?
questions.note: Shipped in Ainalrami 0.30.0: --players, --rounds, --full-bye-pct, --half-bye-pct, --zero-bye-pct, --forfeit-win-pct, --double-forfeit-pct, --odd-results-pct, --acceleration=baku, --tie-breaks (cli.ex:432-458,1510-1525; generator.ex:450-534). Percentages, not per round (optional).

questions.asks: Unset generator parameters get sensible random values?
questions.note: Since Ainalrami v0.37.0 (the pinned version): -g draws unset byes, forfeits, odd results, Baku and a 1-4 item tie-break list, each switched on with --unset-chance (default 50%) from modest ranges (deps/ainalrami generator.ex draw_unset/1, cli.ex unset_option/1, default random); --unset=fixed brings back the corpus defaults. Test: generator_unset_test.exs 'unset options are drawn (Q25)'.

questions.asks: Generator has at least one way to set ratings?
questions.note: Random ratings.

questions.asks: Generator ratings user-specified?
questions.note: --ratings=2400,2350,... per TPN (cli.ex:236-257; generator.ex:414-419). Ainalrami 0.30.0.

questions.asks: Generator ratings parametrised (min/max, gaps)?
questions.note: --rating-range=LOW-HIGH, or --rating-top/--rating-step/--rating-sigma (cli.ex:259-279; generator.ex:421-425). Ainalrami 0.30.0.

questions.asks: Generator ratings random?
questions.note: Uniform 1400..2700 from the seeded RNG when no rating option is given (generator.ex:412).

questions.asks: Same parameters always give the same TRF?
questions.note: Since Ainalrami v0.37.0 a fresh seed is drawn per run without --seed, written into the 012 line and printed, and --seed repeats the run (generator_unset_test.exs 'a seed per run (Q30)'). Ainalrami branch vcl-pass2 (379e4e0) takes that seed from the OS random source (:crypto.strong_rand_bytes) for the Swiss, team and round-robin generators; it needs a new Ainalrami tag and pin to reach OpenPairings.

questions.asks: Generated tournaments follow the pairing rules AND the tie-break list in the file?
questions.note: Every round is paired by the engine; with --tie-breaks the file carries 202 and final ranks by Ainalrami.Tiebreaks (generator.ex:114-129,541-558). The generator writes the engine dialect (XXR), not TRF26.

questions.asks: Generated results follow FIDE rating-table probabilities?
questions.note: Since Ainalrami v0.37.0, -g results follow the FIDE rating table by default with the rating difference limited to 400 (generator.ex results_config, capped_difference, @rating_cap 400); the uncapped table stays as :fide_uncapped for older corpora. Tests: generator_unset_test.exs, Q32.

questions.asks: Tested against another public engine, 50,000+ tournaments each way, pairings AND tie-breaks?
questions.note: Pairings both ways against bbpPairings and tie-breaks both ways against TieBreakServer, over 50,000 tournaments each way (deps/ainalrami/docs/validation.md:17,20,24,1429-1440,1592-1606).

questions.asks: More than 10 discrepancies either way?
questions.note: YES: pairings differ twice (bbpPairings' own [C2] defect), but tie-breaks differ 147,873 times in direction 1 and 2,039 in direction 2, every one classified as a TieBreakServer finding (A-D) or a reading difference (validation.md:17,1605-1606; docs/finding-tiebreakserver-2026-09.md). Routes through Q35-Q39.

questions.asks: Discrepancies caused by our engine?
questions.note: No group of discrepancies was traced to our engines (validation.md; finding-tiebreakserver-2026-09.md).

questions.asks: Discrepancies caused by the other engine?
questions.note: Yes: bbpPairings' [C2] defect, Gacrux's 5.2.5 and TieBreakServer's findings A-D.

questions.asks: Other-engine faults reported?
questions.note: bbpPairings [C2] went to TEC in the 2026-09-08 letter (docs/tec-feedback-2026-09.md:35-52) and upstream (docs/tec-call-questions.md:147-149); Gacrux 5.2.4 was reported upstream (deps/ainalrami/docs/finding-gacrux-5-2-4.md:3). Not on record as sent: the confirmed Gacrux 5.2.5 finding (only an 'offer it' item, tec-call-questions.md:139; the letter predates it) and TieBreakServer findings A-D (finding-tiebreakserver-2026-09.md). Needs a dated sent message for each, or this is NO (25%). See docs/vcl4thp/questions.md.

questions.asks: Discrepancies from different readings of the rules?
questions.note: Yes: some tie-break differences are readings, not errors (e.g. STD), per finding-tiebreakserver-2026-09.md.

questions.asks: Reading differences reported to TEC?
questions.note: Only covered if the tie-break reading differences go to TEC; the 2026-09-08 letter predates them. NO costs 50%.

questions.asks: FIDE mode is the default?
questions.note: Every departing setting ships at the FIDE value (compliance.ex @departures) and a new tournament is Swiss. Caveat: an account can set Keizer as its own default (user_live/settings.ex:939); those tournaments start outside FIDE mode, stamped round 0.

questions.asks: A way to enter FIDE mode?
questions.note: Not needed: default.

questions.asks: Can the program leave FIDE mode?
questions.note: Three ways out: saving a departing setting (tournaments.ex stamp_compliance_loss), a pairing moved by soft rules, extra points or a bye exclusion (pairing.ex record_pairing_deviations), and Leave FIDE mode on Settings > FIDE (tournaments.ex:1014).

questions.asks: Level-4 warning when leaving FIDE mode?
questions.note: Every way out of FIDE mode shows TEC's Level-4 double confirmation first (warn, then 'stay in FIDE mode?'), and only the second confirmation acts; cancelling changes nothing. Explicit exit (settings_fide_live.ex), settings saves through SettingsSupport.fide_gate/5 and Tournaments.fide_departures/2 (options, scoring, pair-by-category), and a pairing moved by soft rules, a bye exclusion or preference or extra points, rolled back until confirmed (Pairing fide_departure_guard). Tests: fide_departure_gate_test.exs.

questions.asks: ### comment in the TRF when leaving FIDE mode?
questions.note: The TRF26 export writes '### FIDE mode exited @ Round N' (or 'before Round 1 was paired') after the header whenever fide_compliance_lost_round is set (trf_export.ex; test/pairings_engine/fide_mode_locks_test.exs) - in copies and TRF26 downloads, not in the file sent for rating, which holds only records by the arbiter's decision (SWAR parity).

questions.asks: Can FIDE mode be re-entered?
questions.note: fide_compliance_lost_round is never cleared, a restore only moves it earlier (tournament_import.ex earliest_compliance_loss), and Compliance.fide_mode?/1 needs it nil (compliance.ex:332). Caveat: a JSON backup import takes the file's value.

questions.asks: Permanent indication when not in FIDE mode?
questions.note: Every page of a tournament not in FIDE mode carries a 'Not in FIDE mode' line linking to Settings > FIDE (layouts.ex:444; fide_mode_live_test.exs).

questions.asks: Imports TRF06?
questions.note: One parser covers TRF06-era files; old-style byes are read as byes (deps/ainalrami/lib/ainalrami/trf.ex:2005-2010; trf_import.ex:1136-1147).

questions.asks: Reports every adjustment TRF06 -> TRF26?
questions.note: The import names the file's version (TRF06/TRF16/TRF26, TrfImport.detect_version/2) and lists every default it used and every old-style bye it converted on a review step before anything is created (TrfImport.adjustments/3, review/2; tournaments_live.ex trf_review). Tests: trf_import_adjustments_test.exs.

questions.asks: Imports TRF16?
questions.note: TrfImport.import_text/2 over Ainalrami.Trf.parse (trf_import.ex:71-76).

questions.asks: Reports every adjustment TRF16 -> TRF26?
questions.note: Same review step: each missing 162/192/202/212/142 is reported with the default used (trf_import_adjustments_test.exs, 'what a TRF06/TRF16 file cannot say').

questions.asks: Imports a defective TRF anyway?
questions.note: Defects are imported: dangling opponents become byes, a wrong points column is a warning, illegal rounds are imported as recorded (trf_import.ex:1136-1147,1437-1458,1498-1504).

questions.asks: Tells the user every adjustment made?
questions.note: Every adjustment is listed before confirming: defaults, dropped tie-breaks and deputies, clamped cycles, unknown 192 codes, ignored 362 and 299 records, 299 switching on counted extra points, one-sided games and F byes turned into byes, rounds not checked, and a crashed verification is reported instead of swallowed (TrfImport.adjustments/3, round_entry_adjustments; tests in trf_import_adjustments_test.exs incl. 'a crash is reported, not swallowed'). Findings are stored with the tournament (import_findings).

questions.asks: Shows the issues when a TRF26 cannot be imported?
questions.note: Off our path (Q51 YES). A refused file shows why: parse error, duplicate ranks, several 012 lines, validation text (trf_import.ex:149-157,318-396).

questions.asks: Checks imported rounds against the pairing rules?
questions.note: Every imported round is replayed: explain_round, Alternatives.violations, bye_eligibility (trf_import.ex:1530-1533,1584-1653). Limits: absolute criteria only, Dutch files only.

questions.asks: Level-3 warning AND ### when imported rounds broke the rules?
questions.note: Imported rounds that break a pairing rule stop the import at a Level-3 review ('Import anyway' or Cancel) before the tournament exists; on confirm the finding is stored (import_findings), logged as a pibe.import audit row and written as '### Import @ Round r' in TRF26 reports, never in the file sent for rating (trf_export.ex import_pibe_comments). Tests: trf_import_adjustments_test.exs, tournaments_live import review test.

questions.asks: In FIDE mode automatically after import?
questions.note: No import sets a departing setting (trf_import.ex:539-570,686-712). Risk: positive 299 records switch on counted extra points, and the next pairing then leaves FIDE mode (pairing.ex record_pairing_deviations).

questions.asks: Round count changeable after the start?
questions.note: In FIDE mode the number of rounds (and a round robin's cycles) cannot change once round 1 is paired, and Unlock does not open it (tournaments.ex:979 @fide_locked, ensure_unlocked/3:1122; fide_mode_locks_test.exs). Leaving FIDE mode first is the way to change it.

questions.asks: Level-4 warning on that change?
questions.note: Off our path: the change cannot happen in FIDE mode (Q57), so YES by the legend.

questions.asks: ### for the change?
questions.note: Off our path: cannot happen in FIDE mode (Q57).

questions.asks: Re-checks the last round when its final/non-final status flips?
questions.note: Off our path: cannot happen in FIDE mode (Q57).

questions.asks: Level-3 + ### if that makes pairings wrong?
questions.note: Off our path: cannot happen in FIDE mode (Q57). YES itself costs 7% if reached.

questions.asks: Warns before start if the setup cannot finish within the rules?
questions.note: Before round 1 the Pairings page warns when the rounds set cannot be paired for the players entered: a Swiss over n-1 rounds (even field) or n (odd), a round robin whose rounds differ from its schedule (Tournament.setup_warnings/2, Tournaments.setup_warnings/1; #setup-warning-*). Tests: setup_warnings_test.exs.

questions.asks: Manual/semi-automatic pairing to finish such a tournament?
questions.note: When the engine proves no legal pairing exists, the Pairings page offers to create the round by hand behind a Level-3 confirmation (#pair-by-hand, Pairing.create_round_by_hand/1): an empty round with every player in the pool, finished by pool pairing and 'Give the pairing-allocated bye' (Tournaments.award_pool_bye/4), then the end-of-session check, recorded as an MPA PIBE. Tests: manual_pairing_test.exs 'three players, four rounds', manual_pairing_live_test.exs.

questions.asks: Pairings can be created or edited by hand?
questions.note: Swap seats or colours, substitute from the pool, vacate/fill a seat, award a bye, pair two pool players, delete an empty last board - each confirmed as a board diff (tournaments.ex swap_players_in_round, pair_from_pool; pairings_live.ex:638-804).

questions.asks: Clear start and end of a manual-alteration session?
questions.note: Hand edits to a round are a session with an explicit start (#mpa-start-N, or the first applied edit) and end (#mpa-end in #mpa-banner); the next round cannot be paired while one is open; audit codes pairing.mpa_started / pairing.mpa_finished (lib/pairings_engine/manual_pairing.ex; rounds.mpa_session). Tests: manual_pairing_test.exs 'a session with a start and an end (Q65)'.

questions.asks: Level-3 on rematch / prohibited / ineligible PAB / triple colour during MPA?
questions.note: Each staged hand edit is checked for a rematch, a prohibited pair, a PAB to a player who had a PAB, a forfeit win or a full-point bye, and three same colours or a difference over two before the last round; the warnings are listed and Apply needs an explicit tick, also enforced on the server (ManualPairing.warnings/4; #confirm-rule-warnings, #confirm-rule-ack). Tests: manual_pairing_test.exs, manual_pairing_live_test.exs.

questions.asks: Warning when both players get the wrong colour?
questions.note: A board where both players get the colour opposite to the one each is due raises a :wrong_colours warning in the same Level-3 block (ManualPairing.warnings/4). Test: manual_pairing_test.exs 'both players getting the colour opposite'.

questions.asks: Check at the end of the session against the correct pairings?
questions.note: Finishing the session runs the pairing checker (the engine on the round as seated) and compares its pairs, colours included, with the round's (ManualPairing.assess/2). Tests: manual_pairing_test.exs 'boards that are not the checker's', 're-entered and put back'.

questions.asks: Level-3 + ### when they differ?
questions.note: When they differ, a Level-3 dialog shows the checker's pairing, the differences, any rule breaches and the line to be written, and needs a tick (#mpa-end-dialog, #mpa-ack); confirming stores rounds.mpa_pibe and TRF26 reports carry '### MPA @ Round r: <checker pairs> => <round pairs>', never the file sent for rating (trf_export.ex mpa_comments/3). Test: 'the TRF carries the PIBE as a ### line; the file sent for rating does not'.

questions.asks: Standard 1/0.5/0 scoring by default?
questions.note: 1 / 0.5 / 0, bye 1 by default (tournament.ex:122-125).

questions.asks: Other scoring systems definable?
questions.note: Free win/draw/loss values on Settings > Scoring (settings_scoring_live.ex:257-291).

questions.asks: 3-1-0 definable?
questions.note: 3-1-0 can be typed in; standings read the values live (standings.ex:1154-1156).

questions.asks: Custom scoring definable?
questions.note: Any value per result (tournament.ex:1127).

questions.asks: Can two draws be worth more than a win plus a loss?
questions.note: Two draws worth more than a win plus a loss is a Compliance departure (:draws_outscore_win, compliance.ex:167): saving it takes the tournament out of FIDE mode, so in FIDE mode it cannot be set (fide_mode_locks_test.exs).

questions.asks: Scoring changeable during the tournament?
questions.note: In FIDE mode the scoring (team match points included) cannot change once round 1 is paired; no Unlock (tournaments.ex:979, ensure_unlocked/3; settings_scoring_live.ex disabled inputs; fide_mode_locks_test.exs).

questions.asks: Re-checks already-paired rounds after a scoring change?
questions.note: Off our path: cannot happen in FIDE mode (Q75).

questions.asks: Level-3 + ### if that makes pairings wrong?
questions.note: Off our path: cannot happen in FIDE mode (Q75). YES itself costs 7% if reached.

questions.asks: Points already played follow the new scoring?
questions.note: Points are worked out from the stored results with the current values on every read (standings.ex:644-663,1154-1156; standings_cache.ex keyed by the tournament).

questions.asks: PAB can be worth a win?
questions.note: bye_value, 1.0 by default (tournament.ex:109; standings.ex:655).

questions.asks: PAB can differ from a win?
questions.note: Its own input on Settings > Scoring (settings_scoring_live.ex:284-291).

questions.asks: PAB can be worth MORE than a win?
questions.note: A bye worth more than a win is a departure (:bye_above_win, compliance.ex:172), so not in FIDE mode (fide_mode_locks_test.exs).

questions.asks: PAB can differ from both win and draw?
questions.note: 0 or any value below a win is allowed (settings_scoring_live.ex:285-290).

questions.asks: Standard scoring with a PAB other than 1, 0.5, 0?
questions.note: Under 1-1/2-0 a bye other than 1, 1/2 or 0 is a departure (:bye_not_a_game_score, compliance.ex:177) (fide_mode_locks_test.exs).

questions.asks: Non-standard scoring: PAB values reachable by standard results?
questions.note: Free value: 2 under 3-1-0 stays in FIDE mode (fide_mode_locks_test.exs).

questions.asks: PAB value changeable during the tournament?
questions.note: In FIDE mode the bye's value (and SWAR presence points on it) cannot change once round 1 is paired; no Unlock (tournaments.ex:979; fide_mode_locks_test.exs).

questions.asks: Re-checks paired rounds after a PAB change?
questions.note: Off our path: cannot happen in FIDE mode (Q85).

questions.asks: Level-3 + ### if that makes pairings wrong?
questions.note: Off our path: cannot happen in FIDE mode (Q85). YES itself costs 7% if reached.

questions.asks: Earlier PABs re-scored to the new value?
questions.note: Every PAB is scored at the current value on every read (standings.ex:655,1055-1101).

questions.asks: Pairing systems besides the Dutch?
questions.note: Round robin (Berger), team round robin, team Swiss C.04.6; Keizer leaves FIDE mode (tournament.ex:5,14).

questions.asks: Other Swiss systems?
questions.note: Team Swiss C.04.6 through Ainalrami.TeamPairing (team_swiss.ex). The only individual Swiss is the Dutch.

questions.asks: Swiss system without a TAPC selectable?
questions.note: C.04.6 can be selected and no program is known to hold a C.04.6 TAPC; YES only routes to Q92.

questions.asks: Rules printable/obtainable for a non-Handbook Swiss system?
questions.note: Every Swiss selectable in FIDE mode is in the Handbook (Dutch, C.04.6); Keizer is not a Swiss and leaves FIDE mode.

questions.asks: Pairing system changeable once underway?
questions.note: pairing_system freezes with round 1 and in FIDE mode Unlock does not open it (tournaments.ex:979, ensure_unlocked/3; settings_options_live.ex locked_hint_message with fide_path; fide_mode_live_test.exs).

questions.asks: Round robin selectable?
questions.note: 'Round robin (Berger)' is a FIDE pairing system here (compliance.ex).

questions.asks: Round-robin TPNs assignable by hand?
questions.note: Before round 1 of an individual round robin the Players page's Starting numbers dialog sets the Berger numbers: move up/down, type a number, draw all by lot (after a confirmation) or reset to rating order; stored in players.pairing_number, used by round 1, locked once a round exists; a later entrant gets the next number (lib/pairings_engine/starting_numbers.ex; round_robin.ex ensure_frozen). Tests: starting_numbers_test.exs, starting_numbers_live_test.exs.

questions.asks: Berger tables?
questions.note: Circle-method Berger tables, single and double, checked against C.05 Annex 1 and SWAR's generator (round_robin.ex:8-45,253-294).

questions.asks: Manual round-robin pairing (no Berger)?
questions.note: Not reached: Q96 YES.

questions.asks: Double RR: choose whether to reverse the last two rounds of cycle 1?
questions.note: A double round robin has a setting to reverse rounds m-1 and m of cycle 1 (rr_reverse_last_two, tournament.ex:672; checkbox settings_options_live.ex:758-772, locked after round 1), on by default for a new double round robin (tournaments_live.ex:1720-1727); applied in round_robin.ex:253-294 (schedule/4, swap_last_two). Tests: round_robin_cycles_test.exs:47,82,272,325. Q99 is off our path.

questions.asks: Always reverses those two rounds?
questions.note: Off our path since Q98 is YES. If reached: the reversal is a setting, default on for new double round robins (round_robin.ex:253-294), not forced.

questions.asks: Manual round-robin pairing possible?
questions.note: Next to 'Pair the whole tournament (Berger)', 'Pair round N by hand…' (#rr-pair-by-hand, behind a tick in #mpa-rr_round-dialog) creates the next round empty (RoundRobin.create_round_by_hand/1) inside the Swiss manual pairing alteration: paired from the not-playing list, a player left off the boards gets the table's zero-point bye at the end (RoundRobin.record_sitting_out/1). Finishing compares the round with the Berger table's round (ManualPairing.assess/2, RoundRobin.table_round/2); a round that differs needs a Level-3 tick and is written '### MPA @ Round r: <table pairs> => <round pairs>' in TRF26 reports, never the rating file (as Q69). Individual round robins over one table only (RoundRobin.by_hand?/1): team, per-category and match-format round robins keep the table. Tests: manual_round_robin_test.exs, manual_round_robin_live_test.exs.

questions.asks: Checks each pair meets once/twice?
questions.note: Every hand-made board is checked against the other rounds of its cycle (a pair meeting twice in one cycle: :rr_repeat, Level-3 tick while editing), and finishing checks that the pairs still to meet split exactly into the cycle's remaining rounds - a 1-factorisation search, the odd-field bye as a phantom opponent (:rr_incomplete; ManualRoundRobin.warnings/4). Pairing the rest from the table is refused when its next round would repeat a pair in the cycle (RoundRobin table_conflict). Tests: manual_round_robin_test.exs 'everyone meets everyone once per cycle (Q101)', manual_round_robin_live_test.exs.

questions.asks: Non-Berger double RR: no three same colours?
questions.note: A hand-made round-robin board giving a player the same colour in three consecutive rounds raises :rr_colour_three (Level-3 tick while editing, listed again at the end; ManualRoundRobin.warnings/4) - for every hand-made round-robin round, single or double; the Berger table itself never does it within a cycle (tested for 3-16 players). Tests: manual_round_robin_test.exs 'no three same colours in a row (Q102)', manual_round_robin_live_test.exs.

questions.asks: RR standings exclude results of players under 50% of games?
questions.note: C.05 6.6(2): a round-robin player withdrawn or expelled having completed (played over the board) under half of their scheduled games is left out of the standings - their games count for nobody's points or tie-breaks, they are listed last without a place; the cross table, norms and the TRF keep every game (Standings.uncounted_withdrawals/2; standings page, print and crosstable show 'withdrawn, not counted'). Tests: round_robin_withdrawal_standings_test.exs (incl. exactly 50% and the TRF).

questions.asks: RR tie-breaks (DE, BPG, BWG, REP, STD, SB, SB/C1-2, RTNG, WIN, TPN, KS variants) correct?
questions.note: The round-robin set is selectable: DE, DE/P, BPG, BWG, REP, STD, SB, SB/C1, SB/C2, RTNG, RTNG/R, TPN, TPN/R, WIN, KS and KS/L1, KS/L2, KS/L-1, KS/L-2 (tiebreaks.ex catalogue; ainalrami_bridge.ex), each compared with Ainalrami's value; the Buchholz family is refused in round robins. Test: tiebreak_families_test.exs 'round robin: the tie-breaks of the checklist's list'.

questions.asks: Buchholz-type tie-breaks usable in RR?
questions.note: Buchholz-type codes can be picked but standings drop them for a round robin and say why (standings.ex:153-160; tiebreaks.ex:174-185); FB/AOB do not exist. They still appear in the TRF's 202 list.

questions.asks: Baku acceleration correct?
questions.note: Fixed in 0.72.0: engine rows are numbered by pairing number (in_pairing_number_order, pairing.ex:4694) and Group A's virtual points ride on its rows (accelerations/3 pairing.ex:4291-4326, accelerated_rows :1679-1690), so brackets are ordered by score plus virtual points, then TPN. Group A is frozen at round 1, 2*ceil(N/4) (freeze_baku_group_a pairing.ex:291-314, baku_group_a_last :4441-4455). Tests: baku_order_test.exs, baku_reference_test.exs (every round compared with bbpPairings and Ainalrami, seeds 1-200, zero differences).

questions.asks: Other acceleration methods?
questions.note: Only none/Baku in FIDE mode; extra points as acceleration is a departure (pairing.ex pairing_deviations).

questions.asks: Rules for other methods printable?
questions.note: Off our path (Q107 NO): no other method in FIDE mode.

questions.asks: Acceleration removable after round 1?
questions.note: In FIDE mode acceleration freezes with round 1, no Unlock (tournaments.ex:979; settings_options_live.ex disabled select; fide_mode_locks_test.exs).

questions.asks: Acceleration changeable after round 1?
questions.note: Same lock as Q109.

questions.asks: Percentage groups respect round-1 byes having no TPN?
questions.note: A player absent from round 1 of a Baku event (requested bye, absence, later start round) holds no TPN at round 1 and is not in N; they are numbered on arrival as a late entry per C.04.2 2.4, after the field or by rating as the tournament says, and the last GA participant stays the same (C.04.7 1.3.2). pairing.ex baku_numbering_pool/3, release_baku_round_one_absentees/3; baku_group_a_test.exs "a round-1 absentee".

questions.asks: All pairing-integrity events logged?
questions.note: Pairing-integrity events are identified, stored and logged as PIBEs: hand edits (MPA, rounds.mpa_pibe, audit pairing.mpa_finished), imports (import_findings, pibe.import), result corrections after a later round was paired (pairings.corrected_from, pibe.correction), TPN exchanges and regenerations (audited), full-point byes and rating-only corrections (audited, ### lines). Tests: manual_pairing_test.exs, trf_import_adjustments_test.exs, long_event_and_correction_live_test.exs, tpn_test.exs.

questions.asks: PIBEs written to the TRF as ###?
questions.note: Each logged PIBE kind is written to the TRF26 report as a ### line: MPA, Import, Correction, FPB, Rating correction (trf_export.ex), never in the file sent for rating.

questions.asks: A PIBE can be undone automatically?
questions.note: A restore point is taken before every PIBE: pairing, unpairing, imports, hand edits (session start), and since this pass a result correction (Snapshots.capture 'pibe.correction'). Test: long_event_and_correction_live_test.exs 'asks first, then takes a restore point and logs the PIBE'.

questions.asks: Level-3 before finalising a PIBE?
questions.note: Every PIBE asks first (Level 3): hand edits (rule-warning tick, MPA end dialog), imports (review step), corrections of an earlier round (:result_correction acknowledgement, #confirm-correction-<id>), TPN exchanges and regenerations, postponed non-draws. Tests as for Q112.

questions.asks: Separate official vs tournament rating?
questions.note: fide_rating is the official rating (TRF 001); the pairing rating is fide_rating, or national_rating when there is none (player.ex:12-16,728-736). Weak YES: a FIDE-rated player cannot get a separate tournament rating.

questions.asks: Custom rating lists?
questions.note: Administrators load rating lists of their own from a CSV file (id, name, rating; optional federation, title, birth year, FIDE ID), validated row by row and previewed before loading; lists are machine-wide, appear in the add-player search and can be put in a tournament's rating-list sequence (lib/pairings_engine/rating_lists.ex, rating_lists/csv.ex, live/rating_lists_live.ex). Tests: rating_lists_test.exs, rating_list_sequence_live_test.exs. The consistency check compares FIDE ratings only.

questions.asks: Effective Rapid/Blitz lists?
questions.note: rating_for_tempo falls back to the standard rating when rapid or blitz is missing - the Effective Rapid/Blitz lists (fide.ex:133-141; rating_refresh.ex:83).

questions.asks: Type-A lists (known source)?
questions.note: FIDE list from ratings.fide.com, KBSB list from the federation's public file (fide/sync.ex:1-5,35; federations/bel/sync.ex:77).

questions.asks: Type-B lists (unknown source)?
questions.note: Off our path. No list of unknown origin can be imported.

questions.asks: All official FIDE lists as Type-A?
questions.note: The combined players_list.zip brings standard, rapid and blitz in one sync (fide/sync.ex:103-135; fide/fide_player.ex:9-11).

questions.asks: All official FIDE lists importable as Type-B?
questions.note: Off our path (only from Q120 YES).

questions.asks: Default rating-list sequence per tournament type?
questions.note: A tournament without its own sequence uses the draft's default for its rate of play (standard: FIDE Standard, Rapid, Blitz; rapid: Effective Rapid, FIDE Blitz; blitz: Effective Blitz, FIDE Rapid) (RatingLists.default_sequence/1). Tests: rating_lists_test.exs 'the default sequence'.

questions.asks: User can define/modify the sequence?
questions.note: The sequence is defined or changed per tournament on its FIDE settings page (#rating-sequence: add, reorder, leave out, reset). Tests: rating_list_sequence_live_test.exs 'the sequence editor'.

questions.asks: Only one list at a time?
questions.note: One FIDE list per tournament, picked by its rate of play, plus the national fallback (fide.ex:135-141; player.ex:728-736).

questions.asks: Sequence editable (exclude, add, reorder)?
questions.note: Lists can be left out (not the last), reordered, and the national, Effective and custom lists added (settings_fide_live.ex). Tests: rating_list_sequence_live_test.exs.

questions.asks: Rating auto-assigned from the main list?
questions.note: The main list of the sequence supplies the rating when a player is picked (players_live.ex pick -> RatingLists.main_values).

questions.asks: Shows ratings in other lists when not in the main one?
questions.note: The add-player search shows the main-list rating for the tournament's rate of play, or says there is none, plus the player's ratings in the other lists (players_live.ex #fide-result-<id>-other). Tests: players_live_test.exs. Picking one of those other ratings (Q129) is still not offered.

questions.asks: User can pick one of those?
questions.note: Each rating the player has in another list of the sequence is a button in the add-player search (#fide-result-<id>-use-<entry>) that fills that rating and records its list. Test: rating_list_sequence_live_test.exs 'picking a rating from another list'.

questions.asks: Minimum rating entered automatically when none found?
questions.note: No automatic minimum rating (player.ex:13,728-736); routes to Q131.

questions.asks: Rating enterable by hand?
questions.note: Free FIDE and national rating inputs on the add form (players_live.ex:2591,2484).

questions.asks: Assigned rating editable?
questions.note: Editable in the edit dialog at any time (players_live.ex:3325,3199).

questions.asks: Consistency checks (are ratings still current)?
questions.note: Refresh ratings re-looks-up every player by FIDE ID and proposes each difference (rating_refresh.ex:60-88).

questions.asks: Source list kept per rating, and manual entry marked?
questions.note: Each FIDE rating keeps its source list and month (players.fide_rating_source, fide_rating_period, fide_rating_listed; migration 20261007090000); a rating typed by hand has no source and one changed by hand is flagged (Player.rating_manual?/1), shown on the player. Tests: rating_refresh_test.exs 'source of an applied rating (VCL4THP 134)', players_live_test.exs. Not covered: the national rating.

questions.asks: Local FIDE lists never more than a day old while running?
questions.note: While the program runs, Fide.AutoSync asks FIDE once a day whether a newer list exists (HEAD, Last-Modified) and runs the existing sync only then; on by default, switchable on Connections (meta.fide_auto_sync); silent and retried when offline (lib/pairings_engine/fide/auto_sync.ex). Tests: fide/auto_sync_test.exs, fide/freshness_test.exs.

questions.asks: One-click update of all local lists?
questions.note: One sync replaces standard, rapid and blitz together (fide_live.ex:327-333).

questions.asks: Consistency check uses the list valid at start (or check date if >30 days)?
questions.note: Each sync records the list month (meta.fide_list_period); the check uses the list valid at the tournament's start, or the check date when the event runs over 30 days, and refuses to compare against a different month, saying why (RatingRefresh.dry_run). Tests: rating_refresh_test.exs 'which list the check uses (VCL4THP 137)'. Only the current list is kept, so an event that started in an earlier month is not compared.

questions.asks: Consistency checks can be switched on/off?
questions.note: Consistency checks can be switched off per tournament on the FIDE settings page (tournaments.rating_checks_enabled, #rating-checks-enabled, default on): no automatic notice, the manual Refresh ratings still compares. Tests: rating_lists_test.exs 'consistency checks on and off'.

questions.asks: Automatic consistency check after a list update?
questions.note: After a list update the check runs at the first opportunity: opening Players or Pairings, or the update finishing while one is open, shows a notice when ratings on file differ from the list (RatingRefresh.notice/1, PairingsEngineWeb.RatingNotice, #rating-check-notice). Tests: rating_refresh_test.exs 'notice/1 (VCL4THP 140)', players_live_test.exs. Routes to Q141.

questions.asks: Consistency check only on request?
questions.note: Off our path while Q139 is YES. The check also runs without being asked (the notice of Q139).

questions.asks: Checks the lists are current before a requested check?
questions.note: A requested check first asks FIDE whether the local list is current (Fide.Freshness.check/0); if stale, an administrator gets the update first and the check follows, others are told to ask an administrator; unreachable FIDE is said. Test: rating_refresh / players_live 'a requested check asks FIDE first'.

questions.asks: Affected players reported?
questions.note: Each affected player with old and new values (players_live.ex:2960-2989).

questions.asks: Ratings updated automatically?
questions.note: Nothing is written until Apply (players_live.ex:1070-1082).

questions.asks: User can update a chosen subset?
questions.note: Each proposed change has a checkbox (ticked by default) with select all; Apply selected writes only the ticked ones (RatingRefresh.select/2, apply/2; #rating-refresh-apply). Tests: players_live_test.exs 'choosing which proposals to apply'.

questions.asks: Tournament-rating methods FIDE/NRO/FIDON/NIDOF/HBFN/OTHER?
questions.note: All six TRF26 tournament-rating methods can be chosen per tournament (FIDE, NRO, FIDON default, NIDOF, HBFN, OTHER; Tournament.rating_methods/0, Player.rating/2; Settings > Options #rating-method-select); HBFN and OTHER read a typed players.tournament_rating. The method drives pairing numbers, the rating-based tie-breaks, team seeding and the published rating. Tests: tournament_rating_test.exs 'each method reads its own rating', tournament_rating_live_test.exs.

questions.asks: Tie order beyond alphabetical for equal rating/title?
questions.note: Players level on rating are ordered by FIDE title (C.04.2 2.2.2: GM, IM, WGM, FM, WIM, CM, WFM, WCM), then by an announced criterion: alphabetical (default), FIDE ID, oldest or youngest first (Pairing.initial_order/2, Player.title_rank/1; #initial-order-tiebreak-select). Tests: tournament_rating_test.exs 'players level on rating are ordered by FIDE title before their name'.

questions.asks: TPNs changeable without editing ratings?
questions.note: Until round 4 is paired, the Players page's Pairing numbers dialog of an individual Swiss exchanges the numbers of two players of equal tournament rating or regenerates them from the ratings (lib/pairings_engine/tpn.ex). Tests: tpn_test.exs, tpn_live_test.exs. Routes to Q148.

questions.asks: TPN exchange only among equal tournament ratings?
questions.note: An exchange is refused between players of different tournament ratings (Tpn.exchange/3, :different_ratings; two unrated count as equal). Test: tpn_test.exs 'players of the same rating exchange numbers; different ratings are refused'.

questions.asks: Level-3 when an exchange breaks the seeding rules?
questions.note: Off our path; vacuous - no exchange exists.

questions.asks: Level-3 on any TPN exchange?
questions.note: Every exchange asks for confirmation first (Level 3, the themed confirm dialog); after round 1 it also says the rounds already paired used the old numbers (players_live tpn modal). Test: tpn_live_test.exs.

questions.asks: TPN exchange/regeneration after round 4 paired?
questions.note: No exchange or regeneration once round 4 is paired (Tpn.editable?, guard_pairing_number_freeze). Test: tpn_test.exs 'nothing changes once round 4 is paired'.

questions.asks: Level-4 if so?
questions.note: Off our path (Q151 NO).

questions.asks: TPN regeneration before round 4?
questions.note: 'Regenerate from ratings' renumbers the field by the current tournament ratings until round 4 is paired (Tpn.regenerate/1). Test: tpn_test.exs.

questions.asks: Level-3 when regeneration moves two or more TPNs?
questions.note: A regeneration that would change two or more issued numbers first lists old and new numbers for confirmation. Test: tpn_live_test.exs 'a regeneration that moves numbers asks first'.

questions.asks: Regeneration keeps the tie-order chosen at first?
questions.note: Regeneration sorts by tournament rating and keeps the current order of equal ratings (which the title and announced criterion gave, Pairing.initial_order/2). Test: tpn_test.exs 'regeneration follows a rating change and keeps the order of equal ratings'.

questions.asks: Late entry after round 4 gets a correct TPN?
questions.note: With 'Late entrants' pairing numbers: By rating' (a per-tournament Swiss setting), a late entrant at any round gets the number their rating earns and everyone below moves down one; played boards are untouched and Baku's Group A line follows its player (Pairing.number_late_entrants/4, ensure_pairing_numbers/2). Tests: tournament_rating_test.exs 'a Swiss late entrant numbered by rating (C.04.2 2.4)' incl. ainalrami -c on every round. By rating is the default for new tournaments (Tournament schema default 'rating'; tournament_rating_test.exs 'a Swiss late entrant rated above the field, late_entry_numbering nil, is number 1'). Choosing 'After the field' ('after') is a FIDE-mode departure behind the Level-4 double confirmation (Compliance.departed?(:late_entrants_after_field, t); fide_departure_gate_test.exs 'late entrants after the field (VCL4THP Q156)'; compliance_test.exs 'late entrants numbered after the field, chosen, is a departure'). Tournaments from before the default keep the migration's 'end' (same numbering, grandfathered, not a departure), as does a JSON backup without the key (TournamentImport.legacy_late_entry_numbering/1; tournament_rating_test.exs 'a JSON backup keeps what it says, and one from before the key is grandfathered'). Printed pairings and standings show the tournament rating (PrintController player_rating/2, rating_header/1; print_controller_test.exs 'the rating printed is the tournament rating (VCL4THP Q156)').

questions.asks: A game can be recorded as adjourned?
questions.note: With postponed games on (Settings > Scoring), *W/*B on the Pairings page, the phone and CSV (results.ex:105-113,152; tournaments.ex update_pairing_result).

questions.asks: Can it pair with results missing?
questions.note: An open * never blocks pairing; blank boards block the normal button and a second one records them as * and pairs (pairing.ex:154-183,422-430).

questions.asks: Missing results auto-recorded as adjourned?
questions.note: Confirmed blank two-player boards of the last round are written as * before pairing, and put back if the pairing fails (postponed_games.ex:244-258,349-377).

questions.asks: Level-2 warning for that?
questions.note: A confirmation before, enforced on the server, then a notice and an audit row (pairings_live.ex:3480-3510; postponed_games.ex:56). Stronger than Level 2.

questions.asks: Final standings with results missing?
questions.note: Standings shown or printed while a game has no result, or a * is open, say they are not final (Tournaments.count_missing_results/2 tournaments.ex:5796; components/postponed.ex:399; print_controller.ex postponed_banner; fide_mode_live_test.exs). Was split: blanks used to print with no warning.

questions.asks: Results for adjourned games enterable any time?
questions.note: A postponed game's result can be entered and corrected in any round; it is exempt from FIDE mode's round window (tournaments.ex:5373 ensure_result_round_open; fide_mode_locks_test.exs).

questions.asks: Level-3 when an adjourned result is not a draw?
questions.note: Replacing * with a non-draw is refused until confirmed, for every writer (postponed_games.ex:302-320; pairings_live.ex:921-929).

questions.asks: Adjourned game marked in the ITDX file?
questions.note: Open * is written as ? on both players' 001 lines in the TRF26 download and copies (trf_export.ex); the file sent for rating writes it as not played, 0000 - Z (0.74.0).

questions.asks: Marked with ??
questions.note: ? in 001, and 162's X at the draw value so the points column adds up (trf_export.ex).

questions.asks: Unknown result symbols imported as unknown?
questions.note: Any other symbol in a result column of a 001 record that names an opponent is rewritten to ? before the parser sees it (TrfImport.rewrite_unrecognised_results/1, called from build_structs_with_data/1) and imported as a postponed game; the opponent's playing code in that round is set to ? too, since the parser demands both sides agree. Each rewrite is an adjustment (TrfImport.unrecognised_result_adjustments/1, rendered by tournaments_live.ex trf_adjustment_text :unrecognised_result: player, rank, round, code) on the review step, so nothing is imported unless the arbiter confirms; Cancel imports nothing. A symbol in a round with no opponent (0000) is not a game and stays refused, before the parser, with a message naming the player, starting rank, round and symbol (TrfImport.check_no_stray_results/1). Ainalrami stays strict. Tests: trf_import_odd_results_test.exs.

questions.asks: Provisional score other than a draw allowed?
questions.note: Draw by default; win or loss only as a departure (compliance.ex :postponed_*_not_draw).

questions.asks: Level-2 when pairing with an older adjourned game open?
questions.note: A confirmation naming the open games before pairing, enforced on the server (postponed_games.ex:261-273; pairing.ex:154-166).

questions.asks: Final standings/TRF with an adjourned game open?
questions.note: In FIDE mode no TRF (copy, engine dialect, file for rating, Send) that holds the round of a postponed game without a result, and no final standings (Standings page, printed individual and team standings), are made: TrfExport.export/3 asks PostponedGames.ensure_reportable/2 with the file's rounds, the pages ask PostponedGames.final_standings_refused?/2, and each refusal lists the open games. The way on without a result is 'Not played in this event' (Settings, Export; PostponedGames.report_not_played/2): Level-4 double confirmation, leaves FIDE mode (fide_compliance_lost_round stamped, audit row), written 0000 - Z in the file for rating and as '### Not played @ Round r' in TRF26 copies (trf_export.ex not_played_comments). A real result keeps FIDE mode. A file of only the rounds before the open game's round (e.g. the rating inbox's copy of an earlier round) is still made, it reports nothing about that game; OpenResults keeps publishing standings marked not final (a design decision, not a final-standings document). Tests: postponed_fide_mode_test.exs (incl. 'a file of only the rounds before its round is made; one that includes it is not'), postponed_fide_mode_live_test.exs.

questions.asks: Withdrawal shown in the standings?
questions.note: A withdrawn player is marked in the individual standings (standings_live.ex withdrawn badge, #player-withdrawn-<id>) and in the standings, Keizer and crosstable prints (print_controller.ex status_note). Test: vcl_small_items_live_test.exs.

questions.asks: Non-zero score for an unpaired player?
questions.note: Absences score abs_value, the PAB bye_value (standings.ex:644-680).

questions.asks: Half-point bye?
questions.note: A half-point bye is an absence with absence points at 1/2 (standings.ex:662,674-680); written as H, the half-point bye, by Pairing.unplayed_code/2 (it was Z with 162 Z=0.5 until 2026-10-02).

questions.asks: Two or more half-point byes?
questions.note: Unlimited unless abs_nbfois caps it (standings.ex:674-691).

questions.asks: Level-3 on the second and later half-point bye?
questions.note: A second or later half-point bye shows a warning in the player dialog and asks for confirmation before saving; the confirmation is in the audit row (Tournaments.second_half_bye_rounds/2, PairingsEngine.HalfByes; players_live #player-half-bye-warning). Tests: half_byes_test.exs.

questions.asks: Players can be marked ineligible for half-point byes?
questions.note: A player can be marked not eligible for half-point byes (players.no_half_bye, #player-no-half-bye); a half-point absence is then refused (Tournaments guard_half_bye_eligibility). Tests: half_byes_test.exs. Routes to Q176.

questions.asks: HPB assignable to an ineligible player?
questions.note: A marked player cannot be given a half-point bye: update_player refuses it, also when it is picked under "Ask the bye type for each absence" (guard_half_bye_eligibility; half_byes_test.exs, bye_types_test.exs).

questions.asks: Full-point bye assignable?
questions.note: A full-point bye is its own kind (byes type 'full-point', never a PAB), given from a paired round's not-playing list (Tournaments.award_full_point_bye/3, withdraw_full_point_bye/3); scored as a win, sent to the engine as F so the player cannot get the PAB later, read from a TRF's F and 240 F. Tests: full_point_bye_test.exs, full_point_bye_live_test.exs.

questions.asks: Level-2 saying full-point byes are deprecated?
questions.note: Before a full-point bye is applied the confirmation shows a Level-2 notice that the pairing regulations do not describe it and it should stay exceptional (#confirm-level2); the player dialog shows the same notice when one is picked for a coming round under "Ask the bye type for each absence" (#player-fpb-notice). Tests: full_point_bye_live_test.exs, bye_type_choice_live_test.exs.

questions.asks: ### for a full-point bye?
questions.note: The TRF26 report writes '### FPB @ Round r: n=FPB' and the 001 record '0000 - F' (trf_export.ex). Test: full_point_bye_test.exs 'written F, with a ### line'. Like every ### line, not in the file sent for rating; see docs/vcl4thp/questions.md.

questions.asks: Odd over-the-board results (1/2-0, 0-1/2, 0-0)?
questions.note: 1/2-0, 0-1/2 and 0-0 can be entered (results.ex:94-99,152).

questions.asks: Inconsistent results (1-1/2, 1-1)?
questions.note: Only codes in the Results table are accepted; 1-1 and 1-1/2 do not exist (results.ex:89-114).

questions.asks: Invalid forfeits (1/2F-0F ...)?
questions.note: No drawn forfeit code (results.ex:96-98).

questions.asks: Only 1F-0F, 0F-1F, 0F-0F as forfeits?
questions.note: Only 1-0FF, 0-1FF and 0-0FF (results.ex:96-98,152).

questions.asks: Mixed standard/forfeit results?
questions.note: No code mixes a played result with a forfeit (results.ex:89-114).

questions.asks: Unrated results (game under one move)?
All enterable results handled correctly?
questions.note: One classification table drives standings, tie-breaks, engine input, export and import (results.ex:89-114).

questions.asks: Boards ordered by the published rules?
questions.note: The engine's output order already follows C.04.2:3.6 (higher score of the higher-ranked player, then sum of scores, then lower TPN, bye last) and plan_boards numbers it in that order (pairing.ex:881-891). Test: board_order_c0402_test.exs (14, 15 and 22 players, 5 rounds, varied results). JaVaFo not checked.

questions.asks: With acceleration, ordered by real + fictitious points?
questions.note: With Baku acceleration the boards come in C.04.2:3.6 order on real plus virtual points; test board_order_baku_test.exs (16 players, rounds 1-3, checked against 3.6 with Group A's virtual points, and shown to differ from real points alone).

questions.asks: Can results/pairings/colours of ANY earlier round be changed?
questions.note: In FIDE mode only the round before the last played, and later ones, can be changed: results, hand edits, team forfeit decisions, and deleting a player who played a closed round are refused (Tournaments.ensure_round_editable/2 tournaments.ex:5772-5779, sent_round_gate/2:5727, ensure_result_round_open/2:4778; team_matches.ex:159; fide_mode_locks_test.exs).

questions.asks: Of the round before the last one played?
questions.note: The round before the last played stays open (tournaments.ex:5772-5779; fide_mode_locks_test.exs).

questions.asks: Of rounds before the second-to-last?
questions.note: Rounds before the second-to-last played are closed in FIDE mode (tournaments.ex:5772-5779; fide_mode_locks_test.exs).

questions.asks: Corrections recorded for the rating report only (C.04.2:4.3)?
questions.note: A result found wrong after the next round is over can be corrected for the rating report only (C.04.2:4.3): pairings.rating_result beside the board's result, which pairings, engine input and standings keep using; the TRF report writes the corrected result (Tournaments.set_rating_correction/3, Pairing.rating_history/1; 'Correct for rating...' on the Pairings page). Tests: rating_correction_test.exs, rating_correction_live_test.exs.

questions.asks: ### noting results used differ from 001 records?
questions.note: The TRF26 report adds '### Rating correction @ Round r: a-b: old => new (pairings and standings used old)' (trf_export.ex). Test: rating_correction_test.exs. Not in the file sent for rating, which carries the corrected 001 results; see docs/vcl4thp/questions.md.

questions.asks: Prohibited pairings supported?
questions.note: Prohibited pairs and club/federation exclusions for the whole tournament, written as 260 (tournaments.ex add_forbidden_pairing; trf_export.ex). No per-round prohibition.

questions.asks: Only before round 1 is paired?
questions.note: In FIDE mode every prohibition - forbidden pairs, pairing rules by club, federation or group, hard or 'if possible' - is set before round 1 is paired, as C.05 5.2 asks of any restriction. Once round 1 is paired, adding, changing or removing one (and changing how hard the wishes are tried, while there are any) asks TEC's Level-4 double confirmation first (SettingsRestrictionsLive ask/3, fide_exit_dialog), then leaves FIDE mode in the same transaction: the act is recorded in tournaments.prohibition_changes and the round under way stamped in fide_compliance_lost_round (Tournaments.record_prohibition_change/2, record_soft_position_change/2). The TRF26 copy writes '### Prohibition @ Round r: ...' beside '### FIDE mode exited @ Round n' (trf_export.ex prohibition_comments); never in the file sent for rating. What a rule announced before round 1 does to a late entrant is not an act and records nothing; prohibitions added late before 0.79.0 are not re-judged (only new acts count). Tests: prohibitions_fide_mode_test.exs, settings_restrictions_live_test.exs 'FIDE mode'.

questions.asks: Addable after a round has been played?
questions.note: In FIDE mode, no: once round 1 is paired any prohibition added, changed or removed takes the tournament out of FIDE mode behind the Level-4 confirmation, stamped and written as '### Prohibition' in TRF26 copies (see Q195). The club/federation rules are pairing rules now and follow the same path. Outside FIDE mode it can be added at any time and is still listed in the TRF26 copy. Tests: prohibitions_fide_mode_test.exs 'once round 1 is paired, in FIDE mode'.

questions.asks: Expelled player can be flagged?
questions.note: A player can be marked expelled (status 'expelled', Player.expelled?/1, #player-expelled; presence column 'E'); expelled players are not paired (every pairing path takes active players only).

questions.asks: Expelled player excluded from standings?
questions.note: Expelled players are left out of the standings after the tie-breaks are computed, so their results still count for their opponents (standings.ex build_standings).

questions.asks: All Swiss tie-breaks in C.07 usable (AOB, APPO, APRO, ARO cuts/medians, BH/FB cuts/medians, BPG, BWG, DE, DE/P, PS cuts, PTP, REP, RTNG, SB cuts, STD, TPN, TPR, WIN, WON)?
questions.note: All 39 C.07 individual Swiss tie-breaks are selectable (tiebreaks.ex catalogue, ainalrami_bridge.ex), written to 202 in C.07 spelling and read back; each is compared with Ainalrami's own value and ainalrami -c accepts a file with a mixed list. Tests: tiebreak_families_test.exs.

questions.asks: Tie-break list changeable during the tournament?
questions.note: In FIDE mode the tie-break list freezes with round 1, no Unlock (tournaments.ex:979; settings_tournament_live.ex disabled editor; fide_mode_locks_test.exs).

questions.asks: Level-4 on that change?
questions.note: Off our path: cannot happen in FIDE mode (Q200).

questions.asks: ### with round and previous list?
questions.note: Off our path: cannot happen in FIDE mode (Q200).

questions.asks: Ties allowed at the end?
questions.note: A tournament setting lets players still level after the whole tie-break list share a place (2=) on the standings page, live page, prints and public snapshot; off, they are ordered and numbered as before (shared_places; standings.ex c07_places, place/1). The TRF rank column is unchanged and the checker accepts it. Tests: tiebreak_families_test.exs 'a place shared...', settings_tiebreak_picker_test.exs.

questions.asks: Simulated drawing of lots for ties?
questions.note: 'Draw lots for ties' on the Standings page (#draw-lots, confirmed) reorders only players still level after the whole tie-break list and records the order as the manual ranking, audited as standings.lots_drawn (lib/pairings_engine/tie_lots.ex). Tests: tie_lots_test.exs, tie_lots_live_test.exs.

questions.asks: Tied players rankable by hand?
questions.note: The manual ranking (tournaments.ex manual ranking functions) takes a hand-set order; the drawing of lots feeds the same mechanism.

questions.asks: Repeated drawing of lots gives different results?
questions.note: A repeated drawing of lots gives the same order: it is a function of the players and a per-tournament seed drawn once from :crypto and kept (tournaments.lots_seed, exported with the tournament). Tests: tie_lots_test.exs.

questions.asks: Externally calculated tie-break values enterable?
questions.note: Tie-break 'External value' (EXT): a value typed per player on the Standings page (#external-tiebreak-<id>, players.external_tiebreak, audited), ranking at its place in the list; TRF26 has no record for it, so 202 leaves it out. Tests: external_tiebreak_test.exs, external_tiebreak_live_test.exs.

questions.asks: At least one method for unrated players in rating tie-breaks?
questions.note: A per-tournament rating for unrated players in the rating-based tie-breaks (tiebreak_unrated_rating); empty keeps C.07 Article 10's drop. The bridge sends /U<n> to Ainalrami and 202 carries it (ARO/U1500), read back on import (AinalramiBridge.c07_code/2). Tests: tiebreak_families_test.exs 'an unrated player'.

questions.asks: More than one such method?
questions.note: Three methods for unrated players in rating tie-breaks (tiebreak_unrated_method): a fixed rating, the lowest rating in the field, the average of the rated players; the number used goes to Ainalrami and the 202 line as /U<n>, and ainalrami -c agrees (Standings.unrated_rating/2). Tests: unrated_methods_test.exs.

questions.asks: Flag for tournaments over 30 days?
questions.note: A tournament can be flagged as lasting more than 30 days (tournaments.long_event), suggested when the round dates span more than 30 days (PeriodRatings.spans_over_30_days?/1, #long-event-suggestion). Test: long_event_and_correction_live_test.exs.

questions.asks: Advises against rating tie-breaks for those (C.07:10)?
questions.note: With the flag on and a rating-based tie-break in the list, C.07 Article 10's advice against them is shown (#long-event-rating-tiebreaks). Test: long_event_and_correction_live_test.exs.

questions.asks: Several ratings per player for long events?
questions.note: Each player can hold later ratings with the round each applies from (players.period_ratings, entered on the Players dialog #player-period-ratings). Tests: period_ratings_test.exs.

questions.asks: Ratings linked to rounds?
questions.note: Each rating carries its first round; expected scores (We, W-We) use both players' ratings of each game's round (PeriodRatings.expected_score/4). Test: period_ratings_test.exs 'expected scores count each game'.

questions.asks: Rating tie-breaks per round's rating?
questions.note: Q214 asks whether, when players hold more than one rating, the rating-based tie-breaks can be calculated with the rating valid for each round. C.07 Article 10's note makes the first rating the rule 'unless the specific regulations of the tournament state otherwise' (Q215, required, stays the default); per round is that otherwise, recommended. Settings, Tournament, 'Rating-based tie-breaks use each round's rating' (tiebreak_rating_per_round, long events only, off by default): each opponent counts at the rating they held in the round the game was played, via Ainalrami's Participant.round_ratings (branch rating-per-round) - ARO and cuts, TPR, PTP, APRO, APPO and the ARO working; RTNG and the unrated check stay on the first rating. Tests: period_ratings_test.exs 'per round: each opponent counts', long_event_and_correction_live_test.exs 'per-round tie-break ratings'; Ainalrami tiebreaks_test.exs 'ARO uses each opponent's rating'.

questions.asks: Default first rating (C.07:10)?
questions.note: By default the rating-based tie-breaks use each player's first rating (PeriodRatings.tiebreak_round/1). Test: period_ratings_test.exs.

questions.asks: User chooses which rating?
questions.note: tournaments.tiebreak_rating_round chooses the round whose ratings the tie-breaks use (#tiebreak-rating-round; AinalramiBridge event/3). Test: period_ratings_test.exs.

questions.asks: Final TRF reflects everything that happened, no TRF-defined event left out?
questions.note: The TRF26 report now also writes 172 with National Rating Support records when national ratings rank a player, 299 with its round (000 / 999), 260 from the round a late prohibition was added, and ### lines for corrections, rating-only corrections, full-point byes, MPAs and imports. Already written: final ranks, 202 in C.07 spelling, 152, 222 where encodable, 330, 310. 212 equals 202 here (points always rank first); 222 cannot encode a delay (122 carries the text). Tests: trf_complete_report_test.exs, trf_checker_round_trip_test.exs. See docs/vcl4thp/questions.md on the file sent for rating.

questions.asks: Level-2 warnings can be switched off?
questions.note: No setting turns warnings off (postponed_games.ex:54-79; features.ex:108-168).

questions.asks: Level-2 and 3 warnings can be switched off?
questions.note: Confirmations are enforced in the write path; no switch skips them (postponed_games.ex:328-337).

questions.asks: Level-4 warnings can be switched off?
questions.note: No setting disables a confirmation (postponed_games.ex:328-337).

questions.asks: Level-4 can be relaxed to Level-3?
questions.note: The warnings are fixed in code (postponed_games.ex:54-79).

questions.asks: Chess960 supported?
questions.note: Per-tournament Chess960 setting; the Pairings page draws a uniform random starting position per round with Scharnagl numbering (e.g. 518 RNBQKBNR), stored with the round, shown and printed with the pairings, audited (lib/pairings_engine/chess960.ex; rounds.chess960_position). Tests: chess960_test.exs, chess960_live_test.exs.

questions.asks: Usable without an internet connection?
questions.note: Desktop releases run locally. Verification ends here.

questions.note: Not reached.
